drhp.business: Energy Development Company Limited generates and sells electricity from small hydro power plants and wind mills, and separately holds contract (infrastructure/construction, including bridges and hydro project O&M) and trading divisions. It also owns hydro projects through subsidiaries EDCL Power Projects Limited and Ayyappa Hydro Power Limited, and through an associate, Arunachal Hydro Power Limited.
drhp.expansion: The Company is in the process of developing several hydro power projects, via subsidiaries and associate companies, with financial investment partners, in remote areas of the country. Given India's untapped hydro potential, particularly in the hilly region, the Company plans to add to its capacity in the coming years.

litigation.note: Income tax demand notices for assessment years 2011-12 to 2020-21 are under appellate challenge; also referenced under the basis of adverse opinion in the Independent Auditors' Report on the Standalone Financial Statements (Directors' Report, GENERAL / DISCLOSURE ON INCOME TAX DEMAND section).

risks.note: Stringent norms and cumbersome procedures for environmental and forest clearances lead to delays in obtaining clearances for projects, which may affect capacity addition programs; the single-window clearance system to mitigate this is yet to be implemented.
The process of land acquisition for infrastructure work and project components (including submergence) is cumbersome and time consuming.

Despite extensive surveys, hydro project components such as head race tunnels, power houses, pressure shafts and surge shafts face geological surprises that result in delays and increased project cost.

Water is a state subject in India, leading to inter-state river disputes that can delay or cause abandonment of hydro projects; some projects are in border areas affected by India's international relations.
Most hydro projects are located in hilly terrain, exposing construction schedules to landslides, hill slope collapses, road blocks, floods and cloud bursts.
Unexpected complexities and delays in clearances or execution, for reasons beyond the company's control, may cause variation or escalation in project cost estimates.
Hydro power schemes are capital intensive with long gestation periods requiring huge investments, which are major constraints in exploiting the available hydro potential.
Since water is a state subject, state governments are demanding a higher share of free power and other incentives, which leads to higher tariffs.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- A deteriorating hydro-thermal mix and increase in peak hour shortages and frequency variations are pushing policymakers to focus on hydropower development.
- India has huge untapped hydro potential, especially in the hilly region, which the company plans to tap into.
- Under the government's 2023-2027 National Electricity Plan, no new fossil-fuel power plants are to be built in the utility sector, with non-fossil fuel generation expected to reach around 44.7% of total gross electricity generation by 2029-30.
- The Small Hydro Power programme is now essentially private-investment driven; projects are generally economically viable and private-sector interest is high, with viability improving as project capacity increases.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Stringent norms and cumbersome procedures for environmental and forest clearances lead to delays in obtaining clearances for projects, which may affect capacity addition programs; the single-window clearance system to mitigate this is yet to be implemented.
- The process of land acquisition for infrastructure work and project components (including submergence) is cumbersome and time consuming.
- Despite extensive surveys, hydro project components such as head race tunnels, power houses, pressure shafts and surge shafts face geological surprises that result in delays and increased project cost.
- Water is a state subject in India, leading to inter-state river disputes that can delay or cause abandonment of hydro projects; some projects are in border areas affected by India's international relations.
- Most hydro projects are located in hilly terrain, exposing construction schedules to landslides, hill slope collapses, road blocks, floods and cloud bursts.
- Unexpected complexities and delays in clearances or execution, for reasons beyond the company's control, may cause variation or escalation in project cost estimates.
- Hydro power schemes are capital intensive with long gestation periods requiring huge investments, which are major constraints in exploiting the available hydro potential.
- Since water is a state subject, state governments are demanding a higher share of free power and other incentives, which leads to higher tariffs.
